summary.intent: Fix the `entire skill` command not displaying session data despite the insightsdb containing 2364 sessions, 45 skill_signals, and 520 Skill tool calls.
summary.outcome: Fixed two root causes: (1) a cache invalidation bug where the skilldb cache key didn't account for facet backfill changes, and (2) name resolution failures for LLM-extracted skill names containing spaces or parenthetical suffixes. Added observability via PopulateResult counters and TUI diagnostic display.

repo: The skilldb cache key was `v5:<branch_tip>` — the branch tip only changes on new checkpoint ingestion, NOT when `entire insights` backfills facets (which populates skill_signals). This race condition caused PopulateFromInsightsDB to run to completion with 0 inserts while marking the cache as fresh.

Skill name resolution (ResolveSkillName) used `-` and `:` as word boundary characters but not space or `(`, causing LLM-extracted names like 'superpowers:brainstorming (visual companion)' to fail matching against registered skills.
TestDiscoverSkills failures are pre-existing and not isolated — they pick up real plugin skills from ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ instead of using temp dirs.

The `entire skill` pipeline has no mid-pipeline observability: PopulateFromInsightsDB previously returned only an error, making it impossible to diagnose where rows were being dropped without adding instrumentation.
The insightsdb and skilldb are separate SQLite databases; skilldb is a derived cache populated from insightsdb via PopulateFromInsightsDB.

code.finding: ResolveSkillName rule 3b (parenthetical stripping) and space/`(` as word boundaries were added. Cache version bumped from v5 to v6. PopulateFromInsightsDB now returns (*PopulateResult, error) with per-stage counters.
GetContentFingerprint() added — a lightweight SQL query of row counts from sessions, skill_signals, tool_calls, and facets tables, used to build the composite skilldb cache key.
Empty state now shows pipeline diagnostic counts (signals found, sessions matched, etc.) when 0 sessions are available, sourced from the PopulateResult struct.
Two new tests added: TestResolveSkillName_SpaceBoundary and TestResolveSkillName_ParenthesisStrippedFromLastSegment. Existing tests updated for the new (*PopulateResult, error) return type.

workflow: TDD (RED→GREEN) was applied to ResolveSkillName: writing failing tests first for the boundary-matching edge cases before implementing the fix prevented regressions in the 8 existing test cases.
Verifying that test failures exist on main/before-changes is a useful practice to distinguish pre-existing failures from regressions introduced by the current work.
Returning structured result types (PopulateResult) instead of relying solely on logging makes diagnostic info actionable in the UI without requiring users to inspect log files.

friction: PopulateFromInsightsDB had zero mid-pipeline observability — required extensive manual investigation (bash queries against SQLite, grepping for callers) to confirm 0 rows were being inserted despite no error being returned.
The cache tip matching (`v5:ee8bbd...`) gave a false signal of correctness — it looked like the cache was current when in fact it had been populated with 0 rows and then marked fresh.

PopulateFromInsightsDB had high maintainability index (lint warning) making it a complex function to modify safely; adding counters to all return paths required reading the full function body multiple times.
memorylooptui compilation errors appeared during verification but were unrelated to the changes, requiring extra filtering to confirm only changed packages compiled cleanly.
Multiple iterative reads of cache.go were needed to make precise edits to the large PopulateFromInsightsDB function body, suggesting the function is too large to modify confidently in a single pass.
open_items: TestDiscoverSkills tests are not isolated (they read from ~/.claude/plugins/cache/) and produce pre-existing failures — these should be fixed to use temp dirs for the home directory.
PopulateFromInsightsDB has a maintainability index lint warning — the function is too complex and should be refactored into smaller stages.
The composite cache key uses row counts as a fingerprint, which could theoretically miss changes where rows are replaced (same count, different data) — a hash of content would be more robust.

cmd/entire/cli/permissions/reviewer.go and cmd/entire/cli/root.go appear in the modified files list but are not mentioned in the transcript — their changes should be reviewed to ensure they are intentional.
